note.headline: Netflix bounces to 60.93 into resistance; still below fair value, adds stay lower

summary.thesis: Netflix is a Grade B business with rising margins and cash flow, priced below its 64.9 DCF base, but sales growth is slowing and estimates are being trimmed.
summary.decision: Long-term: add, but only at lower prices. Swing: no trade while the price sits just under resistance in a downtrend.
summary.act_at: Add at 56.81 and 53.83; no buying above 64.9

note.happening: Netflix rose 2.56% to 60.93 and now sits just under resistance at 61.14–61.64. It is also below its falling 20-day (61.63), 50-day (65.95) and 200-day (79.5) averages. No news has come out since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-19.
note.business: The business itself is still improving. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 31.3% from 29.14%. Free cash flow, the cash left after spending, grew to 11.4B from 9.0B. The share count fell 3.35% in a year. What is at risk is growth and the margin peak. Quarterly sales growth slowed to 11.85% from 16.19% two quarters ago. The filings flag that a 31% margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 17–31%, and peaks like that usually fade. Analysts cut this quarter's EPS estimate by 7.3% over 30 days and next year's by 1.1%. Debt of 12.7B against 8.2B cash leaves net debt of 4.4B, which is manageable next to 11.4B of yearly free cash flow. The downtrend and the put/call open-interest ratio of 2.47 (open bets on a fall versus a rise) reflect sentiment, not a change in the business. They make timing harder, but they do not lower what the business earns.

worth.text: At 60.93 the stock trades at 17.3 times trailing earnings and 16.2 times next year's. Its price-to-sales of 5.0 is below the peer median of 6.8 and at the 20th percentile of its own 5-year history. The cash-flow model (DCF) gives 38.59 / 64.9 / 77.72 for bear / base / bull. The own-history price/sales method gives 59.41 / 84.5 / 122.15. The gap between methods comes down to growth. The current price implies free cash flow starts growing at about 13.0% a year. At 10% starting growth the value is 53.83; at 20% it is 80.35. Margins matter too: if operating margin falls to 23% the value is 60.0, about today's price, and at 15% it is 39.64. So the price already assumes growth near today's pace and margins that mostly hold.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing at 10% or more a year, near the 13.0% the price implies, and operating margin stays well above 23%.

decision.timing: The 2027-01-19 report falls after the 2027-01-15 option expiry (which prices an 11.7% move) and before the 2027-02-19 expiry (17.1%). So adds stop at the 53.83 slice before the report, and more buying waits for a report that keeps operating margin near 31.3%.
